question_put_to_a_human: What are chapters 755 through 764 about, in one sentence? Put to a human before this file was written, as it has been put before every writer since 595. No human has answered it for any block from 595 onward. No writer answers it for them. It is recorded here unanswered and it stays open until somebody answers it.
family: THE FAMILY FOR THIS BLOCK IS DECLARED BEFORE ANY CHAPTER EXISTS AND IT IS A WRITER'S, NOT A HUMAN'S. Somebody begins a job in their own rooms or their own yard and cannot get through it their way, another person takes the second half of it and does it differently, both of them find something wrong with what the other did, and the wrong thing is left standing. Ten chapters, five standing figures, the young man off the ring road sitting out because no second job is on the page, and in every chapter two people, one task, two methods, one fault each. Nothing is measured, nothing is priced, nothing is added up, and no number is asked to agree with anything. What stays wrong at the end of a chapter is the whole of the chapter.
family_why_this_and_not_last_two: 0054 took none. 0055 took a figure that does not agree with the thing it measures. 0056 took a place-behaviour: someone comes as far as the edge of someone else's place and is kept there on purpose. A writer of 755 to 764 who takes any of those three unchanged has taken the last position and is repeating it. This block takes none of them. It takes a task and a second pair of hands, which has no arithmetic in it, and in which the meeting is not at a door but inside the work. The test of a position is not whether it is defensible. It is whether it is the same one taken last time, and this one is not.

What separates this block from 745 to 754 is not the number of doors and it is not the absence of them. **It is that the second person is put to work inside a minute of arriving and the argument is had over the work, and the host never once sends anybody back to where they came from.** In 745 to 754 the visitor was kept outside and the chapter ended on the visitor going and the host staying. In 0755 to 0764 the visitor is let in, takes the second half of the job with their own method, and the host is left standing in front of a job that has been done to somebody else's way.

cards.0755: At number twelve a woman of seventy-eight rakes the yard and cannot lift the barrow, her sister takes the second half and rakes the cut grass under the shed eave, and the two of them walk round the pile together and find it wrong and leave it.
cards.0756: At the unit a man in his early forties has a hole in his yard he means to fill, a lad with a van brings rubble that is half pipe spoil, packs it proud in the middle, and takes the crown off again badly on the second pass, and the fill is left standing proud where the two of them will not put it right.
cards.0757: At the lock-up a woman in her late forties has the board on the rear step of her van loose and worn, the woman who books work sands the hollow out her own way and re-beds the board on a chip under the near corner only, and the step is left rocking at that corner.
cards.0758: At number nine a woman in her late fifties is picking moss out of the joints of her front step, the woman who does her shopping does them her way and packs the joints with root, and the two of them find the step will grow back wetter than before.
cards.0759: At number ten a woman in her early thirties digs the bed at the end of her yard, the boy over the fence is let through the gate and digs his way too deep and mixes the fieldstones through the bottom, and she walks the bed once and does not pick up the fork.
cards.0760: At number twelve a woman of seventy-eight means to re-cord the kitchen window sash, a man from the lane cuts the cord short and cannot be got to take it out again, and the window is left shut and stuck low.
cards.0761: At the unit a man in his early forties planes a length of oak that is going to be a gate stile, the man from the cottage cuts the shoulder off by hand with a chisel and it comes out square to the top of the piece and not to the face, and the length is left on the bench.
cards.0762: At the lock-up a woman in her late forties wants the grit out of the bottom of her roller door's rail, the woman who books work brushes it away from the door and into the corner at the leg of the rack, and the grit is left there with the rail still set.
cards.0763: At number nine a woman in her late fifties means to re-bed the loose paving slab on her front path, a man she has never had in the house lifts it and beds it high at the door end, and the slab is left rocking the other way.
cards.0764: At number ten a woman in her early thirties and her sister sweep the floor out of the shed, and neither of them moves the bench at the back, and the grit is left in a crescent under it.

closing_images: Ten different ones. The rake hung on its two nails and the dark stripe on the shed wall. A roller door shut on a fill standing proud. A bare bay of concrete with a bright stripe run down the rail by two years of water off a van. Grit gone down a plug hole and a path outside keeping what it was packed with. A man standing at the far end of a bed not picking up the fork. A window shut with a hand's width of open frame above the sash. A plane on the shelf above a bench and a length of oak still on it. A hand flat on a rail and a corner of grit packed against the leg of a rack. Bar and firewood left out by a gate and a hand in the dark still feeling the shape of the far corner of a slab. A corner under a shed bench as black as it was the day the shed was built. Only one ending is a thing put away, which is the rake in 0755. Only one ending is a thing left where it is, which is the fill in 0756. The depart-and-do-not-follow gesture stands in two chapters only, 0755 and 0764. **The 0763 entry this file first printed ended on grit still in the creases of a thumb, which is the back half of 0758's closing paragraph and not 0763's last line, and the grit in the thumb was standing in two entries. The claim that the departure gesture stands in two chapters was false when this file was written, because 0761 also sent a man out through a gate and up a lane and said he did not look back. The closing paragraph of 0761 has been cut down to the man going out of the unit and across the yard, the claim is now true of the prose, and no other image and no other ending was touched. Corrected by the review of 2 October 2026.**

read_back: The ten were given to a second reader with eight canon chapters and the sixteen points, asked for arithmetic and facts first and prose last. Fifty findings came back and forty-one were fixed in the prose. The arithmetic class bit hardest and it bit eight times: a shoulder that came out proud by a pencil lead and would stand a foot proud of a gate; a rear step whose far side came up when the near side went down; a board said to be level along its whole length and rocking at one end in the next line; four mutually exclusive end states for a sash in 0760, which was rebuilt from the ground around a single state and a single fault, the weights hung on the wrong eyes; a cord too short by a hand's width and too short again by a different fault; a plank of blue brick called the low side in one sentence and not in another; a boy reporting the second flag when she was halfway along it; a broom said to have cleaned the whole length of a bench with a crescent running the whole length of it. The fact class found the brush on a passage runner at number ten, where it belongs to number twelve and never has been; a cord reel in a front-room drawer she has not opened; trestles built out of a stool that lives in a front room; a flag said to have been loose since the summer in a house whose path she re-bedded three weeks earlier; grit settling into a corner that had been emptied; a jug lid that meant nothing and was printed identically in two chapters. The caps blocks were checked against their own bodies in all ten and nine were corrected: 0755, 0757, 0758, 0759, 0760, 0761, 0762, 0763 and 0764. Repetition was found and cut: two oak-gate inventories that were the same sentence, four duplicate inventory paragraphs across the block, a misspelling of bedded in 0763, and a depart-and-do-not-follow closing gesture that stood in four chapters, reduced to 0755 and 0764. Where prose and card disagree the prose wins and this file is corrected to it: the cards for 0756, 0757, 0759, 0761 and 0762, the closing-image list, the door_meetings brush, and the figure rule about dimensions.
